chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr who said:

Al-Hasan ibn Qiyama asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the garment seamed with silk and cotton, where the silk is more than half; can one pray in it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' And Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) used to have gowns from it like that.

key_terms.الْمُلْحَم: Seamed or mixed (referring to the construction of the fabric)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in a silk-cotton mixed garment where silk is the majority?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the permissibility of praying in mixed silk garments (*thawb mulham*) where silk exceeds half the fabric, a point of nuance in Shia jurisprudence regarding the prohibition of pure silk for men. Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) validates this ruling not only through legal reasoning but also by citing his personal practice of wearing such gowns, thereby establishing a precedent for the acceptability of mixed textiles in ritual prayer. This reflects the broader Shia scholarly view that distinguishes between the luxury of pure silk and the practicality of silk-cotton blends.
